architecture.mechanism: A dense, injectable material migrates through the venous system and becomes securely embedded in the right ventricular apex myocardium, where it is retained so stably that imaging can mistake it for an implanted pacemaker lead.
architecture.intervention: Replace the transvenous pacing lead with a leadless pacemaker capsule delivered via the venous system and anchored at the right ventricular apex using an in-situ-curing, biocompatible cement-like fixation that embeds in the myocardium.
architecture.expected_effect: The lead conductor and its stress-concentration fracture modes are eliminated entirely, while the cement-anchored capsule remains fixed at the apex, delivering reliable long-term electrical pacing therapy.
architecture.falsification_test: Implant the cement-anchored leadless capsule in the right ventricular apex of a preclinical model, apply cyclic flexion/tension fatigue equivalent to 10 years of cardiac motion, and serially measure pacing capture thresholds, leadless capsule dislodgement force, and cement integrity; the concept is falsified if capture is lost, the capsule dislodges, or the cement fixation fractures.
